title: Brent crude above $100 and 10-year Treasury yields above 5% give markets a double test
description: This week has basically revolved around two questions for broader markets. The first being can oil prices keep below $100? And the second being can 10-year Treasury yields stay below the 5% mark? Today, we are starting to get an answer to both. And by the looks of it, neither is going in the direction that markets would have preferred. Brent crude is back above $102 after a push higher in overnight trading, while 10-year Treasury yields have broken through 5% to hit 5.11% - the highest since 2007. title: What are the main events for today?
description: EUROPEAN SESSION In the European session, we have the SNB rate decision and the German IFO survey. The SNB is widely expected to keep the policy rate unchanged at 0.00%, so the focus will be on inflation forecast, assessment of the oil shock, CHF intervention language and guidance for 2027. Inflation has surprised to the upside recently but a large part of the increase was energy-related, with petroleum prices up 25.2% YoY. title: France confidence stays weak in September as inflation pressures cloud the outlook
description: The latest business and household confidence data released today: France September consumer confidence 86 vs 85 expected Prior 86 France September business confidence 96 vs 97 expected Prior 98 French consumer sentiment is seen holding steady in September, although still keeping well below the long-term average reading of 100. The details reveal a slight rebound in households' opinion on future standard of living.
